Daily Devotional

December 3

36 Nevertheless they did flatter him with their mouth, and they lied unto him with their tongues. 37 For their heart was not right with him, neither were they stedfast in his covenant. 38 But he, being full of compassion, forgave their iniquity, and destroyed them not: yea, many a time turned he his anger away, and did not stir up all his wrath. 39 For he remembered that they were but flesh; a wind that passeth away, and cometh not again. (Psalms 78:36-39 KJV)

This is relating how the Jews treated God when He brought them out of Egypt, and through the desert, to bring them into the Promised Land. The Jews gave lip service to God, and went through the motions of serving Him, but their hearts had strayed far from Him. They griped and complained about everything, and although God did such miraculous miracles for them, they seemed to forget them within days. The Jews were the ones who broke covenant with God, but even when they did, God many times controlled His anger, and showed mercy to them. It is a great testimony to the love that God has for us humans, to be so forgiving and merciful to us, when we are so ungrateful to Him. We can fault the Jews for their behavior, but how many of us do the same thing? We are not always thankful for the blessings that God gives us, and we tend to forget them in a short while. We need to remember the goodness of God at all times, and be extremely thankful to Him (Psalms 100:4) for all He does for His children.

It is a wonderful truth that our God knows that we are humans, and have many failures and faults. Even though we continually fall short of what God would have us to be (Romans 3:23), He knows that we are prone to failure, and not holy on our own. That is why He had to send Jesus to give us the holiness that we needed to come back into fellowship with Him. We could never do that on our own, as ever since Adam sinned in the beginning (Genesis 3:6), we have been sinful creatures, and not able to be holy ourselves. No matter how hard a person tries to live holy, you can not do it to Gods standard, and only by being born again (John 3:3) through faith in Jesus, can we ever appear holy to God, and be able to commune with Him. What a wonderful salvation our God has provided for us, and we need to praise Him continually for His mercy and grace in dealing with us. Thank you Jesus for our redemption. Thank you Father for your plan of salvation!
